text:
Brock Boeser has a point in nine straight games, and in Vancouver the conversation has turned to his leadership, with Sportsnet writing about him embracing the role in a rebuilding season. The numbers back the production: 24 points in 24 games, 15 of them on the power play, and his ice time is up to 20.7 minutes over his last ten.

The five-on-five picture is rough. Vancouver gets only 34.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level last season, partly because he plays with weak teammates (bottom 6% by their impact). His 20.5% shooting and 4.75 goals of on-ice luck say some of the scoring is borrowed.

So Boeser is two things at once: a power-play shooter whose points are real enough, and an even-strength player on a team that rarely has the puck. The point streak is nice. Whether the Canucks can drive play when he's on at five on five matters more for what this season becomes.
headline: Boeser is carrying a rebuilding Canucks team
